number-systems:
Give 2 marks Give two reasons for a programmer choosing to show binary values in hexadecimal. (May/June 2023, P12)
ReminderThink about the person reading the value, not the computer.
Hexadecimal is shorter, so it takes less space on screen It is easier to read, so mistakes are less likely

Identify 2 marks Identify two more uses of hexadecimal in computer science. (May/June 2024, P13)
ReminderPick two different uses.
HTML colour codes MAC addresses

Give 2 marks Give two ways in which hexadecimal differs from binary. (Oct/Nov 2024, P12)
ReminderEach point should compare both systems.
Hexadecimal is base 16, whereas binary is base 2 Hexadecimal uses 0 to 9 and A to F, whereas binary uses only 0 and 1
twos-complement-questions:
Convert 1 mark Convert 45 from denary into a two’s complement integer of 8 bits. (Feb/March 2024, P12)
ReminderA positive number starts with 0.
00101101

Convert 2 marks Convert 10110111, a two’s complement integer, into denary. Show all your working. (Feb/March 2024, P12)
ReminderThe leftmost place value is −128.
−128 + 32 + 16 + 4 + 2 + 1 = −73

Calculate 2 marks Calculate how the denary integer –32 is held in two’s complement form. Show all your working. (May/June 2024, P12)
ReminderStart with +32, flip the bits, add 1.
+32 is 00100000, which flips to 11011111 Adding 1 gives 11100000

Convert 2 marks Convert +123 from denary to an 8-bit value in two’s complement. Show all your working. (Oct/Nov 2023, P13)
ReminderNo flipping is needed for a positive number.
123 = 64 + 32 + 16 + 8 + 2 + 1 01111011
text-sound-and-images:
Explain 2 marks Explain why a higher sampling resolution gives a more accurate sound recording. (Feb/March 2024, P12)
ReminderLink bits per sample to amplitude.
More bits are used to store each sample so a wider range of amplitudes can be recorded, each more precisely

State 2 marks State the meaning of sample rate and of sample resolution. (May/June 2023, P11)
ReminderOne definition for each.
Sample rate: how many samples are taken each second Sample resolution: how many bits are used for each sample

Give 2 marks A computer converts an email address to binary with Unicode. Give two benefits of using Unicode rather than ASCII. (Oct/Nov 2024, P13)
ReminderThink about how many characters each can hold.
Unicode can represent far more characters, including symbols and emojis It covers many more languages

Explain 5 marks A pianist records a song. Explain how the analogue sound gets recorded and turned into digital data. (Oct/Nov 2023, P11)
ReminderFollow the sound from microphone to binary.
A microphone picks up the sound wave The wave is sampled at set intervals, measuring its amplitude each time The sample rate sets how many samples are taken per second The sample resolution sets how many bits store each sample Each amplitude is converted to its binary value and stored
igcse-compression-lab:
Identify 3 marks An artist is compressing an image file. Identify one lossless way to compress an image and describe how your method works. (Feb/March 2025, P12)
ReminderName it, then give two descriptive points.
Run-length encoding (RLE) Runs of neighbouring pixels with the same colour are identified Each run is stored as the colour value and the number of times it repeats

Give 3 marks Give three advantages of making a file smaller before storing or sending it. (Oct/Nov 2024, P11)
ReminderCover both storage and transmission.
It takes up less storage space It can be transmitted more quickly It needs less bandwidth and uses less of a data allowance

Describe 4 marks Describe the way lossless compression makes a text file smaller. (May/June 2023, P12)
ReminderNothing is thrown away.
A compression algorithm such as run-length encoding is applied Repeated words, characters or patterns are identified They are stored once in an index or table along with how often they occur or where they appear
ig-cs-data-transmission:
Describe 3 marks Describe how a data packet is structured. (May/June 2024, P11)
ReminderThree parts.
A header, with details such as addresses and the packet number A payload, which is the data being sent A trailer, which marks the end and may hold an error check

Explain 3 marks A scanned barcode’s data goes to a stock control system by serial simplex transmission. Explain the way the data is sent. (Oct/Nov 2024, P12)
ReminderExplain both words, serial and simplex.
The data is sent one bit at a time down a single wire or channel in one direction only, from the scanner to the stock system

Explain 5 marks Explain how a file is split into packets and sent across a network. (Feb/March 2025, P12)
ReminderCover the packet structure and the journey.
The file is divided into small packets, each carrying part of the data as its payload Each packet gets a header holding details such as the destination IP address and packet number Routers direct each packet towards the destination, choosing a route Packets may take different routes and arrive out of order When all have arrived, they are put back into order using the packet numbers
ig-cs-error-detection:
Give 2 marks Odd parity with a positive ARQ is one way to detect errors. Give two other methods of error detection. (May/June 2024, P11)
ReminderDo not repeat odd parity or positive ARQ.
Checksum Echo check

Explain 3 marks An employee’s email data is tested with an echo check. Explain how this finds errors. (Oct/Nov 2024, P13)
ReminderSend back, compare, decide.
The receiving device sends a copy of the data back to the sender The sender compares it with the data originally sent If the two do not match, an error has occurred and the data can be sent again

Describe 8 marks A network checks transmitted data using an odd parity check together with a positive automatic repeat query (ARQ). Describe how this system finds errors. (May/June 2024, P11)
ReminderCover parity first, then the acknowledgement and timeout.
Before sending, the 1s in each byte are counted A parity bit is set so that every byte has an odd number of 1s The sender transmits a packet and starts a timer The receiver counts the 1s in each byte If every count is odd, the receiver sends back a positive acknowledgement The sender then transmits the next packet If any count is even, no acknowledgement is sent When the timer runs out with no acknowledgement, the packet is sent again
ig-cs-encryption:
Explain 2 marks Explain the meaning of encryption. (Feb/March 2020, P12)
ReminderWhat happens to the data, and why.
Data is scrambled using an algorithm and a key so that anyone who intercepts it cannot understand it

Describe 4 marks Describe how symmetric encryption differs from asymmetric encryption. (Feb/March 2024, P12)
ReminderCompare the keys.
Symmetric encryption uses one shared key to both encrypt and decrypt the data Asymmetric encryption uses a pair of keys, one public and one private The public key encrypts and only the matching private key can decrypt

Explain 4 marks Explain the process of encrypting data with symmetric encryption. (May/June 2024, P12)
ReminderUse the words plain text, cipher text and key.
The original data is called plain text An encryption algorithm and a key turn it into cipher text The same key is later used to decrypt it so the key has to be shared with the receiver
ig-cs-error-types-compared:
Give 2 marks A check digit and a checksum are two checking methods. Give two ways they are alike. (May/June 2020, P11)
ReminderBoth calculate something.
Each calculates a value from the data and attaches it to the data Each repeats the calculation later and reports an error if the values do not match

Explain 3 marks An employee’s email data is tested with an echo check. Explain how this finds errors. (Oct/Nov 2024, P13)
ReminderSend back, compare, decide.
The receiving device sends a copy of the data back to the sender The sender compares it with the data originally sent If the two do not match, an error has occurred and the data can be sent again

Describe 8 marks A network checks transmitted data using an odd parity check together with a positive automatic repeat query (ARQ). Describe how this system finds errors. (May/June 2024, P11)
ReminderCover parity first, then the acknowledgement and timeout.
Before sending, the 1s in each byte are counted A parity bit is set so that every byte has an odd number of 1s The sender transmits a packet and starts a timer The receiver counts the 1s in each byte If every count is odd, the receiver sends back a positive acknowledgement The sender then transmits the next packet If any count is even, no acknowledgement is sent When the timer runs out with no acknowledgement, the packet is sent again
ig-cs-entry-vs-transmission-checks:
Describe 2 marks Describe how validation differs from verification. (May/June 2020, P21)
ReminderSay what each one can and cannot show.
Validation tests whether data is reasonable, but cannot show that it is correct Verification tests whether data matches the original, but does not test it against any rules

Explain 4 marks Explain why data being input needs both validation checks and verification checks, giving one example of each type. (Feb/March 2020, P22)
ReminderValidation: sensible. Verification: copied correctly.
Validation is needed to check that data is sensible and meets set rules Verification is needed to check that data has not changed as it was entered A validation example is a range check A verification example is double entry

Give 4 marks Give two kinds of verification check, stating how each may be used. (May/June 2023, P23)
ReminderName and use for each.
Visual check The user reads the entered data and compares it with the original Double data entry The data is typed twice and the computer compares the two entries, asking again if they differ
ig-cs-check-digits-modulo-isbn:
Give 2 marks A check digit and a checksum are two checking methods. Give two ways they are alike. (May/June 2020, P11)
ReminderBoth calculate something.
Each calculates a value from the data and attaches it to the data Each repeats the calculation later and reports an error if the values do not match
ig-cs-computer-architecture:
Describe 2 marks Describe what the MDR does during the fetch-decode-execute cycle. (Oct/Nov 2023, P11)
ReminderThink about what it holds and where it came from.
It temporarily holds data or an instruction that has just been fetched from memory, or is about to be written to it

Describe 2 marks Describe what the CPU does in a computer. (May/June 2024, P13)
ReminderProcess instructions.
It processes instructions and data by repeatedly carrying out the fetch–decode–execute cycle

Identify 3 marks Identify one of the buses in a CPU and explain what it does in the fetch–decode–execute cycle. (May/June 2023, P13)
ReminderName, then two points about its job.
Address bus It carries addresses from the processor to memory, so the correct location can be accessed

Give 3 marks Give three registers found inside a CPU. (May/June 2024, P13)
ReminderNames or abbreviations.
Program counter (PC) Memory address register (MAR) Memory data register (MDR)
ig-cs-input-output-sensors:
Identify 2 marks Identify two devices for input that could be built into a smartphone. (Oct/Nov 2024, P11)
ReminderInput devices only.
Touchscreen Microphone

Explain 5 marks A self-driving tractor must stop if a person comes within 3 metres while it is moving. Explain how an infra-red sensor, a microprocessor and an actuator could achieve this. (Feb/March 2024, P12)
ReminderSensor, compare, act, repeat.
The sensor continually sends digitised readings to the microprocessor The microprocessor compares them with stored values for a person and a distance of 3 m If a person is within that distance, the microprocessor sends a signal to the actuator The actuator applies the brakes and stops the tractor Otherwise no stop signal is sent, and the process repeats

Describe 6 marks A farm’s animals drink from a bowl that is refilled automatically once empty. Describe how a sensor and a microprocessor do this. (May/June 2023, P11)
ReminderSend, compare, act, repeat.
The sensor continually takes readings from the bowl and sends the digitised data to the microprocessor The microprocessor compares each reading with a stored value If the reading shows the bowl is empty, it sends a signal to release water An actuator opens the supply for a set time or amount, then closes it The process repeats until the system is switched off
ig-cs-data-storage:
Explain 2 marks Explain why secondary storage is needed in a computer. (May/June 2024, P12)
ReminderCompare with RAM.
It keeps data and programs permanently because it is non-volatile, so nothing is lost when the power is off

Explain 3 marks Explain the reasons why RAM is needed in a computer. (May/June 2024, P11)
ReminderSay what it holds and why that helps.
It stores temporarily the data currently in use and the programs currently running so the CPU can access them much faster than from secondary storage

Describe 6 marks Describe three ways solid-state storage differs from optical storage. (May/June 2024, P12)
ReminderEach difference must mention both.
Solid-state uses electrons held in transistors (NAND or NOR gates), whereas optical uses lasers to read marks on a disc Solid-state is usually faster to read and write, whereas optical is slower Solid-state usually holds more data than an optical disc It has no moving parts, whereas an optical drive spins the disc A solid-state device is likely to be more durable, whereas a disc scratches easily Optical storage is usually cheaper per GB than solid-state
ig-cs-network-hardware:
Give 2 marks Give two ways a MAC address differs from an IP address. (Oct/Nov 2022, P13)
ReminderCompare both in each answer.
A MAC address is set by the manufacturer, but an IP address is given by the network or provider A MAC address normally stays the same, but an IP address can change

Identify 3 marks Identify three features of a MAC address. (Feb/March 2025, P12)
ReminderWho sets it, what it looks like, whether it changes.
It is assigned by the manufacturer It is unique to the network interface card It is usually written in hexadecimal

Describe 3 marks Describe the meaning of a dynamic IP address. (May/June 2023, P11)
ReminderIdentify, change, when.
An address that identifies a device on a network but which can change for example each time the device connects
ig-cs-system-application-software:
State 1 mark State what firmware is for. (May/June 2024, P11)
ReminderOne purpose.
To permanently store the instructions that start up and control the hardware

Give 2 marks Give two examples of software that counts as system software. (May/June 2024, P11)
ReminderNot applications.
Operating system Utility software, such as antivirus

Describe 2 marks Describe how application software differs from system software. (May/June 2024, P12)
ReminderContrast their purposes.
System software runs and manages the computer and provides a platform for other software Application software lets the user carry out particular tasks, such as writing a letter
ig-cs-operating-systems:
Give 2 marks One job of an operating system is handling interrupts. Give two of its jobs that involve memory. (May/June 2024, P13)
ReminderMemory, not interrupts.
Allocating and freeing space in RAM (memory management) Multitasking, keeping several programs in memory without them overwriting one another
ig-cs-running-applications:
State 1 mark State what firmware is for. (May/June 2024, P11)
ReminderOne purpose.
To permanently store the instructions that start up and control the hardware

Give 1 mark Give an example of firmware. (May/June 2024, P11)
ReminderSomething stored in ROM.
The bootloader
ig-cs-interrupts:
Give 2 marks Give two more examples of an interrupt from hardware. (Oct/Nov 2023, P11)
ReminderThe key press is already used.
Moving the mouse A printer running out of paper

Give 2 marks Give two examples of an interrupt from software. (Oct/Nov 2023, P11)
ReminderErrors in running programs.
Division by zero Two processes trying to use the same memory location

Describe 5 marks Describe the way interrupts are used when someone presses a key on a keyboard. (Oct/Nov 2023, P11)
ReminderSignal, priority, queue, service routine.
Pressing the key generates an interrupt signal The interrupt is sent to the CPU and placed in a queue according to its priority The CPU finishes its current instruction and checks the interrupt queue If this interrupt has the highest priority, the CPU runs its interrupt service routine to process the key press It then returns to the task it was doing
ig-cs-high-low-level-languages:
Describe 2 marks Describe the meaning of a low-level language. (May/June 2023, P11)
ReminderHow close is it to the machine?
It is close to the instructions the processor works with such as machine code, or assembly language written with mnemonics

Describe 2 marks Describe the meaning of a high-level language. (Feb/March 2021, P12)
ReminderCompare with machine code.
It uses words close to human language and is focused on the problem It is portable and must be translated into machine code before it runs

Give 3 marks Give three reasons why a high-level language might be chosen over a low-level one for writing a program. (May/June 2020, P12)
ReminderThink about the programmer and portability.
It is easier to read and understand It is easier to debug and maintain The program can be used on different types of computer
ig-cs-assembly-languages:
Give 1 mark Give one advantage a programmer gains from writing a program in assembly language. (Oct/Nov 2024, P11)
ReminderControl over the hardware.
Hardware such as registers and memory can be controlled directly

Give 2 marks Give two disadvantages of writing a program in assembly language. (Oct/Nov 2022, P11)
ReminderDifficulty and portability.
It is hard to learn, write and debug The program is not portable to other types of processor
ig-cs-translators:
Describe 2 marks Describe how errors are reported by a compiler. (May/June 2023, P12)
ReminderWhen and how many.
It reports after trying to translate the whole program listing the errors together, to be fixed before the program can run

Describe 3 marks A programmer translates a program with a compiler. Describe how the compiler does the translation. (May/June 2023, P12)
ReminderHow much, into what, with what result.
It translates the high-level code into machine code translating the whole program before any of it runs and produces an executable file

Explain 4 marks Explain why one programmer might use both a compiler and an interpreter. (May/June 2020, P12)
ReminderMatch each translator to a stage.
Both translate high-level code into machine code An interpreter suits writing the program, because code can be tested and debugged line by line A compiler suits the finished program, producing an executable file which can run without the translator or the source code
ig-cs-compilers-interpreters:
Describe 2 marks Describe how errors are reported by a compiler. (May/June 2023, P12)
ReminderWhen and how many.
It reports after trying to translate the whole program listing the errors together, to be fixed before the program can run

Describe 4 marks Describe two ways an interpreter differs from a compiler. (Oct/Nov 2021, P12)
ReminderTwo differences, each with both sides.
An interpreter translates and runs code one line at a time whereas a compiler translates the whole program in one go An interpreter stops at the first error it meets whereas a compiler reports errors together after translating

Explain 4 marks Explain why one programmer might use both a compiler and an interpreter. (May/June 2020, P12)
ReminderMatch each translator to a stage.
Both translate high-level code into machine code An interpreter suits writing the program, because code can be tested and debugged line by line A compiler suits the finished program, producing an executable file which can run without the translator or the source code
ig-cs-ide:
Identify 3 marks An IDE provides translators. Identify three further functions that IDEs commonly have. (Feb/March 2025, P12)
ReminderDo not include the translator.
Code editor Auto-completion Error diagnostics

Give 3 marks A programmer’s IDE has a built-in compiler. Give three further functions that IDEs commonly have. (May/June 2023, P12)
ReminderDo not include the compiler.
Run-time environment Prettyprint (colouring and layout of code) Auto-correction
ig-cs-software-keyword-workout:
State 1 mark State what an interrupt is for. (Feb/March 2024, P12)
ReminderWho needs to know?
To signal that something needs the processor’s attention

Describe 2 marks Describe how application software differs from system software. (May/June 2024, P12)
ReminderContrast their purposes.
System software runs and manages the computer and provides a platform for other software Application software lets the user carry out particular tasks, such as writing a letter

Describe 2 marks Describe the meaning of a low-level language. (May/June 2023, P11)
ReminderHow close is it to the machine?
It is close to the instructions the processor works with such as machine code, or assembly language written with mnemonics
internet-and-www:
Describe 2 marks Describe how the world wide web differs from the internet. (May/June 2024, P12)
ReminderInfrastructure against content.
The internet is the worldwide network of connected networks and hardware The world wide web is the collection of web pages accessed using the internet

Identify 2 marks Identify two of the parts that make up a URL. (Oct/Nov 2024, P12)
ReminderParts of a web address.
The protocol, such as HTTPS The domain name

Describe 2 marks Describe the chief purpose of a web browser. (Oct/Nov 2023, P13)
ReminderWhat does it do with HTML?
To display web pages by rendering the HTML it receives
how-a-website-loads:
Explain 2 marks Explain the way a website’s URL gets turned into its Internet Protocol (IP) address. (May/June 2022, P13)
ReminderWhich server holds the matches?
The URL is sent to a domain name server (DNS) which looks it up and returns the matching IP address

Describe 3 marks Describe the meaning of HTTPS. (Oct/Nov 2022, P13)
ReminderProtocol plus security.
A protocol, a set of rules, for transferring web pages that is secure, using SSL or TLS so the data is encrypted while it is transmitted

Describe 4 marks A music streaming company has a website. Describe how its web pages are requested and then shown on a user’s computer. (May/June 2021, P11)
ReminderBrowser, DNS, web server, render.
The browser sends the URL to a DNS to find the matching IP address The DNS returns the IP address to the browser The browser uses HTTP or HTTPS to request the page from the web server at that address The server sends the files back, and the browser renders the HTML to display the page
dns-clue-station:
Explain 2 marks Explain the way a website’s URL gets turned into its Internet Protocol (IP) address. (May/June 2022, P13)
ReminderWhich server holds the matches?
The URL is sent to a domain name server (DNS) which looks it up and returns the matching IP address

Describe 4 marks A music streaming company has a website. Describe how its web pages are requested and then shown on a user’s computer. (May/June 2021, P11)
ReminderBrowser, DNS, web server, render.
The browser sends the URL to a DNS to find the matching IP address The DNS returns the IP address to the browser The browser uses HTTP or HTTPS to request the page from the web server at that address The server sends the files back, and the browser renders the HTML to display the page
blockchain-explained:
Identify 1 mark Identify the process that records the use of digital currency on a digital ledger. (Oct/Nov 2023, P12)
ReminderOne word.
Blockchain

Give 2 marks Give two further features of a digital currency. (Oct/Nov 2023, P12)
ReminderThink about its form and control.
It exists only in electronic form It can be decentralised, with no single bank in control

Draw 4 marks Draw and label a diagram showing how blockchain is used when a payment is made in digital currency. (Oct/Nov 2024, P11)
ReminderShow the steps as linked boxes with arrows.
The payer’s device encrypts the payment details and sends them to the digital ledger The payment is recorded there with details such as a time stamp and digital signature It is stored in a block that has its own unique hash The completed block is added to the blockchain, linked to the previous block’s hash, on every device holding a copy
cyber-security:
Describe 3 marks Employee user accounts are attacked by brute force. Describe how such an attack could gain access. (May/June 2023, P11)
ReminderRepeat until it works.
Passwords are guessed by trial and error, often by software with one combination after another being entered until the correct one is found and the attacker can log in

Give 3 marks Give three things that cookies can be used for. (Oct/Nov 2024, P13)
ReminderThree different uses.
Remembering log-in details Keeping items in an online shopping basket Storing preferences so that pages can be personalised

Explain 5 marks A company puts a firewall in place against hackers and malware. Explain how a firewall works to protect the network. (May/June 2024, P11)
ReminderCriteria, examine, decide.
Rules are set, such as lists of allowed and blocked IP addresses The firewall examines traffic coming into and going out of the network Each item is compared with the rules Traffic that does not meet them is rejected Ports that attackers might use can be closed
ig-cs-logic-gates:
State 2 marks NAND, OR, XOR, NOR and NOT are logic gates. State another logic gate and complete a truth table for it. (Oct/Nov 2022, P12)
ReminderOne mark for the name, one for the table.
AND Outputs for AB = 00, 01, 10, 11 are 0, 0, 0, 1

Identify 3 marks Identify which of the AND, OR, NAND, NOR and XOR gates output 1 for each input pair: A = 1, B = 1; A = 0, B = 0; and A = 1, B = 0. (Feb/March 2022, P12)
ReminderWork through one pair of inputs at a time.
A = 1, B = 1: AND and OR A = 0, B = 0: NAND and NOR A = 1, B = 0: OR, NAND and XOR
ig-cs-logic-circuits:
Draw 4 marks Draw a logic circuit for X = (A XOR B) AND (B OR NOT C). Keep the expression unsimplified and give each gate at most two inputs. (Feb/March 2022, P12)
ReminderFour gates, one mark each.
An XOR gate taking A and B A NOT gate on C An OR gate taking B and NOT C An AND gate joining the XOR and OR outputs to give X

Draw 5 marks Draw a circuit of logic gates for X = (A OR NOT B) AND (B AND NOT C), using gates with no more than two inputs and without simplifying. (Feb/March 2023, P22)
ReminderFive gates, one mark each.
A NOT gate on B An OR gate taking A and NOT B A NOT gate on C An AND gate taking B and NOT C A final AND gate joining the OR and AND outputs to give X

Draw 5 marks Draw the circuit for X = (NOT A OR NOT B) OR NOT C with logic gates of two inputs at most, leaving the expression as it is. (Oct/Nov 2023, P23)
ReminderThree NOT gates and two OR gates.
A NOT gate on A A NOT gate on B An OR gate taking NOT A and NOT B A NOT gate on C A second OR gate taking the first OR output and NOT C to give X
ig-cs-truth-tables-expressions:
Write 3 marks A safe (X) opens only when key A and key B are both used (1 = used) and time switch C is off (0). Write a logic expression for this. (May/June 2024, P22)
ReminderOne condition at a time, joined correctly.
A AND B NOT C X = (A AND B) AND NOT C

Complete 4 marks A safe (X = 1 when it can open) needs keys A and B both used (1) and time switch C off (0). Complete its truth table for A, B and C. (May/June 2024, P22)
ReminderEight rows, from 000 to 111.
Rows 000 and 001 give X = 0 Rows 010 and 011 give X = 0 Rows 100 and 101 give X = 0 Row 110 gives X = 1 and row 111 gives X = 0

Complete 4 marks A window opens (W = 1) automatically only if temperature T is too high (1) while heater H is off (0) and air conditioning A is also off (0). Complete the truth table, with inputs in the order A, T, H. (Oct/Nov 2024, P23)
ReminderOnly one row of the eight opens the window.
Rows 000 and 001 give W = 0 Row 010 gives W = 1 Row 011 gives W = 0 All four rows with A = 1 give W = 0
ig-cs-single-table-databases:
Describe 1 mark Describe what a primary key is for. (May/June 2023, P23)
ReminderUnique identification.
It identifies each record in a table uniquely
ig-cs-data-types-primary-keys:
Describe 1 mark Describe what a primary key is for. (May/June 2023, P23)
ReminderUnique identification.
It identifies each record in a table uniquely

Identify 3 marks Identify three of the data types that programs use. (Feb/March 2024, P22)
ReminderAny three of the five in the syllabus.
Integer String Boolean

State 4 marks State the meaning of the integer and real data types, with an example of each. (May/June 2024, P21)
ReminderDefinition and example for both.
Integer: a whole number Example: 27 Real: a number with a fractional part Example: 18.75

Describe 4 marks Describe two data types, string and char, giving an example of each. (May/June 2024, P23)
ReminderDescription and example for both.
String: a group of characters, which may mix letters, digits and symbols Example: "Room 12" Char: a single character Example: ’X’
ig-cs-sql:
Explain 3 marks Explain what each SQL statement does. First: SELECT SUM (Months) FROM Contract; Second: SELECT COUNT (News) FROM Contract WHERE News; (May/June 2024, P22)
ReminderSUM adds values; COUNT counts records.
The first adds together the values in the Months field for all the records in the Contract table The second counts the records in which News is true

Explain 3 marks Explain what these SQL statements do: SELECT SUM (Minutes) FROM Songs WHERE Genre = "rock"; and SELECT COUNT (Title) FROM Songs WHERE Genre = "rock"; (May/June 2023, P22)
ReminderBoth use the same condition.
Only records whose Genre is rock are used The first totals the Minutes field for those records The second counts how many of those titles there are
ig-cs-programming-concepts:
Describe 3 marks Describe the use of variables and constants in a program. (Feb/March 2023, P22)
ReminderCover what they share and how they differ.
Both store data that is reached through a name (identifier) The value of a variable can change while the program runs The value of a constant stays the same

Identify 3 marks Identify three of the data types that programs use. (Feb/March 2024, P22)
ReminderAny three of the five in the syllabus.
Integer String Boolean

Describe 4 marks Describe the meaning of variable and of constant, giving one example of each. (May/June 2022, P23)
ReminderMeaning and example for both.
A variable is a named store whose value can change as the program runs Example: a running total A constant is a named value that does not change as the program runs Example: Pi
ig-cs-selection:
Write 5 marks Write pseudocode that inputs a whole number from 1 to 4 inclusive and uses a CASE statement to output the number entered, or the word “ERROR” if it is outside that range. (May/June 2024, P21)
ReminderInclude OTHERWISE and ENDCASE.
INPUT Number
CASE OF Number
   1 : OUTPUT 1
   2 : OUTPUT 2
   3 : OUTPUT 3
   4 : OUTPUT 4
   OTHERWISE OUTPUT "ERROR"
ENDCASE
The number is input CASE OF and ENDCASE are used with the variable There is a branch for each value from 1 to 4 Each branch outputs the number OTHERWISE outputs ERROR
ig-cs-iteration:
Describe 4 marks Describe two kinds of iteration a programmer can use in a program. (Feb/March 2024, P22)
ReminderTwo loop types, each explained.

ig-cs-string-handling:

Write 4 marks Write pseudocode that changes the string P to upper case, finds where the string Q appears in P (positions start at 1) and stores that position in Position. (May/June 2023, P22)
ReminderConvert first, then search along P.
P ← UCASE(P)
Position ← 0
FOR Index ← 1 TO LENGTH(P) - LENGTH(Q) + 1
   IF SUBSTRING(P, Index, LENGTH(Q)) = Q
     THEN Position ← Index
   ENDIF
NEXT Index

Write 4 marks In pseudocode, write a bubble sort that puts the array Values[1:50] in ascending order. (Feb/March 2024, P22)
ReminderTwo loops, a swap and a stopping condition.
Last ← 50
REPEAT
   Swap ← FALSE
   FOR Index ← 1 TO Last - 1
      IF Values[Index] > Values[Index + 1]
        THEN
           Temp ← Values[Index]
           Values[Index] ← Values[Index + 1]
           Values[Index + 1] ← Temp
           Swap ← TRUE
      ENDIF
   NEXT Index
   Last ← Last - 1
UNTIL NOT Swap OR Last = 1
An outer and an inner loop are used Neighbouring elements are compared They are swapped using a temporary variable The sort stops when no swaps are made
